SMTO-CFG-0082 — SMTO couldn't find the Skill list saved for this Task

GUID: 169813d1-c48e-55b7-9492-4d2a421e8e84
Slug: capability-activation-manifest-unavailable
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: capability_activation

What happened

  • When a Task starts, SMTO saves a list of Skills it may add later. That list isn't available for this Task, so SMTO can't add more Skills to it. Nothing new was turned on.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the Task's finished steps so you know what it already did. The Task may have done part of the work before it needed another Skill.
  2. If you know which Skill the work needs, open Capabilities by the message box and set that Skill to Always. A Skill set to Always is included from the start, so it doesn't have to be added later.
  3. Send a new request for only the work that is still missing. A new request gets its own saved Skill list, so SMTO can add Skills when they're needed.

What success looks like

  • The new request uses the Skills it needs without this message.

If it still fails

  • Send Copy error details to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to force the Skill on in the old Task or delete its saved data; leave that Task as it is.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • On-demand Skill activation found no usable capability manifest in the run's accepted capability ceiling (capability_activation.manifest_unavailable); this retained label has no direct current producer.

What this means

  • This retained manifest-unavailable kind has no direct current producer; current activation relies on the manifest frozen in accepted capability authority. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • This retained manifest-unavailable kind has no direct current producer; current activation relies on the manifest frozen in accepted capability authority.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect retained authority/manifest and the actual activation failure; the label alone does not prove a storage fault.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the run's capability_ceiling.manifest and the actual activation result in the run state (request and classify in src/agent_runtime/native/capability_activation.py); the label alone does not prove a storage fault. Leave the original run unchanged and admit the remaining work as a new task, which compiles a fresh manifest.
  • Preserve the original run state and use supported recovery or new-task admission with a valid manifest after existing work is settled.

Retry and execution caution

  • The reported capability or interaction condition changes.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid accepted manifest supports discovery without inventing tool identities.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass frozen authority, operation permissions or credential requirements.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
